notes:
Flat body confirmed correct: invokeCapability applies each field's own json_path (/test_case/<field>), so sending fields flat (no test_case wrapper) succeeded with 200 every time. The capability's guidance describing a required 'test_case' wrapper at 400 is describing the underlying HTTP contract that invokeCapability's json_path machinery already satisfies for the caller — not a caller-facing instruction to nest, and it was never actually hit as a rejection here, so it is not scored as drift. 

Claim 1 (is_shared): NOT declared as a body param at all -- invokeCapability rejected it client-side verbatim as 'unknown body: is_shared. accepted: <32-field list>' before any HTTP call was made. This means the capability's own guidance text ('is_shared is checked before the write ... and is then discarded, so the value never takes effect. Use the bulk edit to change sharing.') describes server-side behaviour for a field that cannot be sent through this surface at all -- that guidance is unobservable/untestable through update_test_case, a structural limit of this suite rather than a gap in this probe. It is also an internal inconsistency in the authored contract: guidance references a field the declared param list does not carry, consistent with the resolution notes' description of fields added/removed by hand during the twin merge.

Claim 2 (old_id/expectation/attachment_id/ids/issue_tracker/created_at/updated_at): all seven are declared body params (confirmed against the client-side 'accepted:' list). Tested old_id and expectation directly: both accepted with 200 and no error, but neither is echoed by update_test_case's own response nor by get_test_case's read shape -- their effect is genuinely unverifiable through this surface (same structural-limit class as is_shared, but for accepted-not-declared-missing fields rather than an undeclared field). attachment_id was skipped -- no real previously-stored attachment id existed in the fixture and inventing one is out of scope. ids was skipped deliberately: its own description ('ids of other cases this write applies to, for the shared-write path') risks fanning the write out to other cases including the __readonly__ fixtures, which must never be written. issue_tracker was skipped because it is only meaningful paired with issues, which was not sent. created_at was tested with a past date and behaved exactly as the contract claims: no error, no effect (created_at stayed at its original value) -- CONFIRMS the contract for created_at. updated_at, however, DRIFTS from the contract: the contract groups created_at and updated_at together as 'dropped without error when the workspace lacks the entitlement'. In reality updated_at is actively validated server-side -- a past-dated value 400'd with 'updated_at must be greater than or equal to current time' -- and even a valid, future-dated value that passed that check was still never applied (the response's last_updated_at was the server's own current time, not the submitted value). So updated_at is validated-yet-always-discarded, not simply 'dropped without error' like created_at; the contract's claim that the two fields behave the same way is false for updated_at. Additionally, that 400's body was {success:false, message:'...'} with no `error` object at all, disagreeing with this capability's own declared 400 envelope ({success, error:{code,message,details}}) -- a second capability (after the two already on record) failing its declared error envelope, reinforcing the systemic pattern flagged in the standing lessons.

Claim 3 (identifier): contract claims it maps to a third-party identifier only in project-level-id workspaces and is otherwise ignored. Sent identifier=TC-54458 (its own current value) deliberately, to avoid risking the fixture's addressability if the workspace really is in that mode. The response's identifier stayed TC-54458 either way, so this is inconclusive by construction -- genuinely untestable here without risking breaking the fixture, exactly the caveat the contract itself invites; not scored as drift.

Claim 4 (sparse update / empty-string semantics): confirmed omitted fields (status, case_type, automation_status, owner, preconditions, custom_fields, attachments, folder_id, template) kept their stored values across every write in this probe -- sparse-update semantics hold. Empty-string semantics differ by field: description='' actually CLEARS the field to null (verified independently via get_test_case, and last_updated_at advanced, so it was a real write, not a no-op) -- unlike `name`, which the contract says 400s on an empty string rather than clearing. This mirrors the batch-2 finding on update_custom_field that empty strings are a no-op on some fields but a clear on others; here it is a clear.

Fields changed on TC-54458 and restoration status: name, description, priority, tags, and one step's result text were changed and ALL were restored to their original values (confirmed by an independent get_test_case read matching the step-1 baseline exactly, aside from last_updated_at which necessarily advances on every write and cannot itself be restored without triggering another advance). old_id/expectation/created_at/updated_at claim-test values never had a durable, verifiable effect on the case (created_at and updated_at both ended up back at their original/natural values with no restore action needed), so no additional restore was required for them. Verified in storage throughout via independent get_test_case reads (setup steps 1-4), never trusting the update response's echo alone. All preprod calls succeeded on the intended try (no status-0 'could not be reached' retries were needed). No 500s were encountered. Verdict is DRIFT: driven primarily by the updated_at contract violation (validated-with-error rather than silently dropped, plus a non-conforming 400 error envelope) and secondarily by the is_shared guidance/declaration inconsistency; the successful update's own response shape (probe.item_shape) matched its declared nested schema exactly, with no undeclared_returned or declared_missing fields on the 200 path itself.
